definition_en: a place where children go to learn, or to train someone, or a group of fish swimming together

sceneCN: 这里 school 是「学校」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们学校有了一座新图书馆。

senses.title: A place where children go to learn
senses.definition: A place where children go to learn
senses.example: Our school has a new library.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校有了一座新图书馆。

senses.whyCN: school 源自拉丁语 schola，原指学者闲谈的场所，英语保留了学习场所之义。

senses.definition: To train or educate someone
senses.example: The coach schools young players in passing.
senses.why: Because a school trains minds, the noun turned into a verb meaning to train or discipline.
senses.whyCN: 因为学校训练头脑，名词转为动词，指训练或磨炼。

senses.title: A group of fish swimming together
senses.definition: A group of fish swimming together
senses.example: A school of fish moved past the reef.
senses.why: The fish sense came from Dutch schole, a shoal; English borrowed the same spelling for a crowd of fish.
senses.whyCN: 鱼群义来自荷兰语 schole（鱼群），英语以同一拼写借入指成群游动的鱼。

definition_en: to move on foot, to go out for a walk, or a journey made on foot
core_image: 爷爷牵着狗沿河边慢慢走
scene: 爷爷牵着狗沿河边慢慢走 Grandpa walks the dog slowly along the river.

senses.definitionCN: 大学授予的最高学术头衔
senses.example: Her father is a doctor of law.
senses.why: The old sense of a learned teacher survived in the university: the top degree still makes its holder a doctor, teacher of the field.

definition_en: the day of the week between Saturday and Monday
core_image: 阳光照进安静的早晨，一家人准备去礼拜
scene: 星期日我们全家一起去教堂。 On Sunday our whole family goes to church.
sceneCN: 这里 Sunday 是「星期日」（第 1 个义项：一周中星期六与星期一之间的那一天）；句意：星期日我们全家一起去教堂。

senses.title: The first day of the week
senses.definition: the day of the week that comes after Saturday and before Monday
senses.definitionCN: 一周中星期六之后、星期一之前的那一天
senses.example: We go to the park on Sunday.
senses.why: The day is named for the sun, and calendars often place it at the start or end of the week.
senses.whyCN: 这一天以太阳命名，日历常把它放在一周的开头或结尾。

senses.title: The day of rest and worship
senses.definition: the weekly day of rest and religious service in many traditions
senses.definitionCN: 许多传统中每周休息和做礼拜的日子
senses.example: Sunday is a quiet day in our town.
senses.exampleCN: 星期日在我们镇上是个安静的日子。
senses.why: The day carries centuries of religious rest, so its name also means a pause from work.
senses.whyCN: 这一天承载了数百年的宗教休息传统，因此名字也意味着停工歇息。

senses.title: The day in feasts and customs
senses.titleCN: 节庆与习俗中的星期日
senses.definition: the name used for church feasts and weekly customs that fall on this day
senses.definitionCN: 用在这一天举行的教会节庆和每周习俗中的星期日
senses.example: Palm Sunday begins Holy Week.
senses.why: A fixed weekday gathers special names around it, so Sunday also marks feasts and family routines.
senses.whyCN: 固定的星期名会聚拢特别名称，所以 Sunday 也标记节庆与家庭惯例。

intro.en: Sunday is literally the sun's day, a name shared with many Germanic languages.
intro.cn: Sunday 字面上就是太阳之日，这个名字与许多日耳曼语言共享。

items.en: Dies Solis means the day of the sun.

definition_en: to push yourself off the ground, or to rise suddenly
core_image: 一个人屈膝起跳，双脚离地，影子落在下方的地面
scene: 他从地面起跳，双脚离地，影子落在下方。 The children jump over the rope.
sceneCN: 这里 jump 是「跳」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们跳绳。

senses.title: To push off the ground into the air
senses.definition: to push off the ground so that both feet leave it
senses.example: The children jump over the rope.
senses.why: The word's core action is pushing off the ground so that the body leaves it, which is a jump at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心动作是蹬地让身体离开地面，这就是最朴素的「跳」。

senses.title: To rise suddenly and sharply
senses.definition: to increase suddenly and by a large amount
senses.example: Prices jumped last month.
senses.why: A price can leap the way a body leaps: the sudden sharp rise is pictured as leaving the old level in one spring.
senses.whyCN: 价格能像身体一样起跳：突然的猛涨被想象成一跃离开原来的水平。

senses.title: To pass over others without waiting
senses.definition: to move past others or a stage without waiting one's turn
senses.definitionCN: 不按顺序、越过别人或某一环节
senses.example: He jumped the queue at the ticket office.
senses.why: To jump a queue is to leap over the people waiting, using the jump as a way of getting past them.
senses.whyCN: jump a queue 就是从排队的人头上跃过去，借「跳」越过他们。

senses.title: A spring off the ground, as a noun
senses.definition: one act of springing off the ground
senses.example: She won the long jump at school.
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun, so a jump counts one spring or one event built on jumping.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，a jump 就是数一次弹跳，或一项以跳为基础的项目。

definition_en: to make a picture with a pen or pencil, or to pull something
core_image: 一张白纸上，一支铅笔正画出一个圆形的太阳
scene: 一张白纸上，一支铅笔正画出一个圆形的太阳。 She draws a sun on the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 draw 是「画」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她在纸上画了个太阳。

senses.title: To make a picture with a pen or pencil
senses.definition: to make a picture or line with a pen, pencil or similar tool
senses.definitionCN: 用笔之类的工具画出图形或线条
senses.example: She draws a sun on the paper.
senses.why: Old English dragan meant to drag or pull, and dragging a pen across paper left a line, so the pulling sense gave birth to drawing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dragan 意为「拖、拉」，把笔在纸上拖动就会留下线条，「拉」的意思由此生出「画」。

senses.title: To pull something along
senses.definition: to pull something behind or towards you
senses.definitionCN: 把东西往后或往自己这边拖
senses.example: The horse draws the cart up the hill.
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of the word: dragan named the physical act of pulling a load along the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最老的意思：dragan 指把重物沿着地面拖动的动作。

senses.title: To attract people or attention
senses.definition: to make people come or look
senses.definitionCN: 把人引过来或让目光聚过来
senses.example: The singer drew a large crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那位歌手引来一大群人。
senses.why: Pulling and attracting share one picture: something exerts a force and people move towards it, as if drawn by a rope.
senses.whyCN: 「拖」和「吸引」共用一个画面：有东西施加拉力，人就朝它移动，像被绳子牵过去。

senses.title: A result with no winner
senses.definition: an end to a game in which both sides have the same score
senses.definitionCN: 比赛结束时双方得分相同
senses.example: The match ended in a draw.
senses.why: When two sides are evenly matched, neither pulls the other over, so the game is said to end in a draw, as if the rope stayed still.
senses.whyCN: 双方势均力敌时谁也拉不动谁，比赛就成了 draw，好像绳子停在原地。

definition_en: a machine or hand tool that moves air, or a person who admires someone
core_image: 夏天的房间里，台扇转着头送出凉风

senses.title: A machine for air
senses.definition: a machine that moves air
senses.example: Please turn on the fan.
senses.why: Fan for moving air comes from Latin vannus, a winnowing basket that separated grain from chaff in the wind.
senses.whyCN: 表示送风的风扇来自拉丁语 vannus，即扬谷用的簸箕，靠风把谷粒与谷壳分开。

senses.title: A hand tool for cooling
senses.definition: a hand-held object for cooling
senses.example: She waved a paper fan.
senses.why: The same Latin word named the basket waved to make a breeze, and English used it for the hand tool that does the same job.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词指用来扇起风的簸箕，英语就用它指做同样事情的手持扇子。

senses.title: An eager supporter
senses.definition: a person who admires a sport or star
senses.definitionCN: 热爱某项运动或明星的人
senses.example: He is a football fan.
senses.why: This fan is short for fanatic, from Latin fanaticus, 'belonging to a temple'; its heated devotion became the modern sense of an eager supporter.
senses.whyCN: 这个 fan 是 fanatic 的缩写，源自拉丁语 fanaticus「属于神庙的」；那种狂热的投入变成了现代「热心支持者」的意思。

senses.why: Old English sceawian meant to look at; the sense shifted to letting others look, and English kept the everyday verb.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 sceawian 意为观看，后转为让别人看，英语保留了这一日常动词。

senses.title: A performance or a public display
senses.definition: A performance or a public display
senses.example: We watched a magic show at the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在集市上看了一场魔术表演。
senses.why: A show is what is put before an audience to be looked at, so the noun names the performance itself.
senses.whyCN: show 是摆到观众面前供人观看的东西，名词就指这场表演本身。

senses.title: To prove or make clear
senses.definition: To prove or make clear
senses.example: The test shows that he has improved.
senses.why: What is shown becomes evidence; the verb came to mean making a fact clear.
senses.whyCN: 被展示出来的东西成为证据，动词便引申为使事实清楚。

definition_en: a place where people stay in tents or simple shelters
core_image: 湖边搭着几顶帐篷，中间升起一小堆火
scene: 湖边搭着几顶帐篷，中间升起一小堆火。 We camp by the lake for two nights.
sceneCN: 这里 camp 是「营地」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我们在这湖边露营两晚。

senses.title: A place where people stay in tents
senses.definition: a place where people live temporarily in tents or huts
senses.definitionCN: 人们临时搭帐篷或住小屋的地方
senses.example: The camp by the lake was quiet at night.
senses.exampleCN: 湖边的营地夜里很安静。
senses.why: Camp came from Latin campus, 'field', through French, and first named the field where an army set up its tents.
senses.whyCN: camp 经法语来自拉丁语 campus「田野」，最初指军队搭帐篷驻扎的那片野地。

senses.title: To stay in a tent or temporary shelter
senses.definition: to stay outdoors in a tent or temporary shelter
senses.definitionCN: 在户外搭帐篷或住临时住所
senses.example: We camp by the lake for two nights.
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so camp names the act of setting up and staying at such a place.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，camp 表示搭起营地并在那里住下的行为。

senses.title: A side in a dispute or debate
senses.definition: one side in a disagreement, whose members share a view
senses.definitionCN: 争执或争论中观点相同的一方
senses.example: The two camps in the debate never agree.
senses.exampleCN: 争论中的两派从不让步。
senses.why: People who share a view are grouped as if they lived in the same camp, so the word also means a side in a dispute.
senses.whyCN: 观点相同的人被看作住在同一个营地里，于是这个词也指争执中的一方。

items.cn: 拉丁语 campus 意为「田野、平地」。

items.en: The word first named a soldier's field base.

items.en: Later it named any stay in tents.
items.cn: 后来它指任何住帐篷的户外停留。

items.en: Camp names tents, holidays and groups.
items.cn: 现代英语中它指帐篷、假期活动与阵营。
